meta.description: Designs QC, corrects signal drift, removes batch effects, filters features, normalizes samples, and imputes missing values for untargeted LC-MS/GC-MS metabolomics, framing each step as a measurement model that can create or erase biological signal.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, p-values, or effect sizes across any of the 9 outputs; all references in SKILL.md are real, checkable citations.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive medical conclusions; data-processing skill with no individual-subject claims.

methodological_ground.detail: RE-AUDIT: the pre-fix FAIL (impute.QRILC on raw, non-log intensities silently emitting negative intensities) is fixed and verified. Input 3 re-ran the EXACT pre-fix repro (seed 5/9, same 17-feature diagnosed-MNAR subset): the fixed log2()-then-QRILC-then-2^x pattern from SKILL.md's Impute section produced 0 negative values across all 310 imputed cells (min=4.76), versus the old pattern's 123/310 negative (min=-776.37) reproduced independently in Input 8 Part A on the identical data. The new stopifnot(min(...)>=0) guard fired correctly when the old (buggy) pattern was deliberately re-run (Input 8 Part A), and passed cleanly on the fixed pattern (Input 3, Input 8 Part B). No other methodological fallacy found across any of the 9 outputs.

code_usability.detail: All 9 inputs' generated R code executed via pmp/imputeLCMD/missForest/sva against the audit-env R 4.4.3 install; no syntax errors or missing-dependency failures. Input 8 Part B shows impute.QRILC failing LOUDLY (not silently) with 'NA/NaN/Inf in y' when fed NaN-contaminated log-intensities from non-positive raw values -- a safe failure mode, not a code defect.

functional_suitability.note: The one pre-fix gap (QCRSC's silent all-NA behavior below minQC undocumented) is now closed: SKILL.md's QC-RSC section documents the failure mode inline and ships a copy-pasteable guard line. Pipeline Order table gained a 5a row clarifying the QRILC log2/2^x round-trip is local to the call, not a step reorder -- verified this reading matches the actual runnable code in Input 3/8.

reliability.note: Both silent-failure gaps identified pre-fix (QCRSC all-NA, QRILC negative values) now ship inline stopifnot guards, both verified to fire correctly on the exact failure conditions (Input 4, Input 8 Part A) and pass cleanly on normal runs (Input 1, 5, 3). Remaining half-point gap: SKILL.md doesn't mention that non-positive raw intensities (possible from imperfect upstream drift correction) make log2()/impute.QRILC fail loudly rather than silently -- a safe but undocumented edge case (Input 8 Part B).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew modestly (new guard lines, 5a table row, Common Errors row) but stayed well-structured; not bloated for the domain's genuine complexity.

agent_usability.note: Decision trees and guard lines map directly to real function names/parameters. The new PQN factor code block (documented flags-attribute AND colData path) removes a prior undocumented-API gap; Input 9 confirms the colData(SummarizedExperiment) path -- the more common real path given xcms-preprocessing's own output type -- works as written, not just the plain-matrix path the fix log itself verified.

human_usability.note: Common Errors table gained a QRILC-negative-values row and clarified the QCRSC all-NA row; strong discoverability and forgiveness unchanged from pre-fix.

security.note: No credential handling or destructive operations; unchanged from pre-fix.

key_strengths: The P0 Research Veto finding is verifiably fixed, not just documented as fixed: re-running the EXACT pre-fix repro data through the fixed log2/QRILC/2^x pattern gives 0 negative values across 310 imputed cells (was 123/310, min=-776.37), and a fresh adversarial test (Input 8) confirms the new guard actually fires when the old mistake is deliberately reproduced -- the guard is a real backstop, not decoration.

Both P1 fixes hold under conditions the fixer's own verification didn't cover: the QCRSC all-NA guard fires correctly on the documented sparse-QC failure (Input 4) and stays silent on three different normal-QC datasets (Inputs 1, 5); the PQN per-sample-factor fix works on BOTH the plain-matrix path the fix log verified AND the SummarizedExperiment/colData path it did not (Input 9) -- the latter being the more common real-world input type.
Research Veto now PASSES on all four dimensions -- this Skill is deployable, unlike the pre-fix audit.

The canonical pipeline still runs end-to-end on real MTBLS79 data with genuine held-out-QC validation (0.2298 -> 0.0780 RSD), and correctly declines to 'fix' an information-theoretically unwinnable batch/group confound (Input 5).

recommendations.title: Permutation-test guardrail still trips at its nominal false-positive rate on clean data
recommendations.problem: Replacing the fixed |r|>0.3 cutoff with a 999-permutation test (the P2 fix) is a genuine calibration improvement, but on this audit's exact clean-case draw the permutation test still reports p=0.022 (TRIPPED) despite the true dilution-group correlation being 0 -- expected behavior for a properly calibrated test at its ~5% nominal rate, but a user seeing one 'TRIPPED' verdict may not realize that.
recommendations.root_cause: usage-guide.md recommends the permutation test but doesn't caveat that any single well-calibrated test will still false-positive at its nominal rate; no guidance on replication or multiple-draw interpretation.
recommendations.fix: Add one line to the guardrail Tips: a single TRIPPED verdict from the permutation test can still occur by chance at ~5% under a true null -- corroborate with the dilution-factor correlation (should be high) before concluding normalization is eating the effect.

recommendations.title: Non-positive raw intensities upstream of QRILC aren't mentioned in Common Errors
recommendations.problem: If any upstream step (e.g. an imperfect drift-correction division) leaves a non-positive value in a feature fed to log2()/impute.QRILC, the fixed pattern fails loudly ('NA/NaN/Inf in y') rather than silently -- a safe failure mode, but undocumented, so an agent seeing this error has no signpost in SKILL.md pointing at the actual cause.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md assumes raw MS intensities are always positive (physically true for a peak table) and doesn't anticipate corrupted input from an earlier buggy step in an agent-composed pipeline.
recommendations.fix: Add a Common Errors row: 'NA/NaN/Inf in y from impute.QRILC -> a feature has a non-positive value before the log2() call, usually from a division-by-near-zero in an earlier drift-correction step; check min(feature_matrix, na.rm=TRUE) > 0 before imputing.'
